concepts.name: Lead Unburying
concepts.description: The practice of restructuring communication so the most important message appears first and receives the greatest emphasis.

concepts.name: Core Reinforcement
concepts.description: Using supporting devices such as analogies, examples, and concrete imagery to strengthen and clarify a core message.

problems.name: Interesting but irrelevant information
problems.description: Communicators include information that attracts attention but distracts audiences from the central message.

insights.author: Chip Heath & Dan Heath
insights.title: Place the core message first
insights.what_it_says: The most important message should appear at the beginning of a communication rather than being hidden beneath supporting details.
insights.why_it_matters: Audiences are more likely to understand, remember, and act on a message when its core idea is immediately visible.

examples_from_source.what_happened: The original article buried the key point about irreversible skin damage beneath background information. The revised version moved the core message to the beginning.
examples_from_source.why_it_matters: The revision made the message clearer and more memorable.
examples_from_source.transferable_lesson: Start communication with the most important idea rather than supporting details.

decision_rules.action: Place the most important idea at the beginning.
decision_rules.rationale: People should encounter the key message before supporting details.

patterns.description: Restructure communication so the core message becomes immediately visible.

warnings.warning: Starting with interesting but secondary information.
warnings.consequence: The audience may miss the most important point.
warnings.prevention: Identify the core message before organizing content.

application_patterns.when_to_use: When creating articles, presentations, reports, campaigns, or educational materials.
application_patterns.adaptation_notes: Works across writing, teaching, leadership, and marketing.

when_not_to_use: Narrative storytelling where suspense is intentionally created
tradeoffs: Leading with the core improves clarity but may reduce narrative buildup.
insights.evidence: Avoid burying the lead. Don't start with something interesting but irrelevant.

insights.author: Chip Heath & Dan Heath
insights.title: Analogies make core ideas more memorable
insights.what_it_says: A core message becomes more understandable and memorable when reinforced with familiar analogies and concrete imagery.
insights.why_it_matters: People understand abstract concepts more easily when they can connect them to existing mental models.

examples_from_source.what_happened: The revised article compared sun damage to aging, emphasizing that both are cumulative and irreversible.
examples_from_source.why_it_matters: The analogy made the abstract concept of long-term skin damage easier to understand.
examples_from_source.transferable_lesson: Use familiar experiences to explain unfamiliar or abstract concepts.

decision_rules.condition: When a core message is difficult to visualize or understand.
decision_rules.action: Connect the idea to a familiar experience.
decision_rules.rationale: Familiar concepts improve comprehension and recall.

patterns.description: Use a familiar comparison to strengthen a core idea.
steps: Link the analogy back to the message

application_patterns.when_to_use: When teaching, persuading, or simplifying complex ideas.
application_patterns.adaptation_notes: Particularly effective for educational, marketing, and leadership communication.

tradeoffs: Analogies improve understanding but may oversimplify complex realities.
insights.evidence: We've added the analogy to aging to hammer home the idea that damage is irreversible.

insights.author: Chip Heath & Dan Heath
insights.title: Remove information that does not support the core
insights.what_it_says: Interesting information should be removed when it distracts from the central message, even if it is factually useful or engaging.
insights.why_it_matters: Every additional detail competes with the core message for attention.

examples_from_source.what_happened: The revised sun exposure article removed information about melanin so the irreversible damage message could stand out.
examples_from_source.why_it_matters: The elimination of supporting mechanics increased focus on the key takeaway.
examples_from_source.transferable_lesson: Not all useful information deserves inclusion if it weakens the main point.

decision_rules.rule: Cut information that does not strengthen the core message.
decision_rules.action: Remove details that are interesting but unnecessary.

patterns.description: Preserve the prominence of the central message by removing competing details.

warnings.warning: Including information solely because it is interesting.
warnings.consequence: The audience may remember the detail rather than the main message.
warnings.prevention: Evaluate every detail against the core objective.

application_patterns.when_to_use: When clarity and memorability are more important than completeness.
application_patterns.adaptation_notes: Useful for content creation, presentations, leadership communication, and product messaging.

tradeoffs: Removing details increases clarity but may reduce depth and nuance.
insights.evidence: We've had to eliminate some interesting stuff in order to let the core shine through.

relationships.evidence: The revised message moved the core message to the beginning.
